cells.tense: You are holding what you carry and the fairness in it is clear to you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are already carrying for someone else and say out loud what it costs you. Then leave it alone for the rest of the day.
cells.core:
You can feel what is fair without arguing it out. It sits in the body as a plain knowing — what is owed, where the line is, which apology would not be true. And you can bear what has to be borne without going hard about it. Either half alone is common. The two together are not.

The balance costs you something to keep: it means not turning that quiet sense of fairness into a running account. You are strong enough to carry the weight. You are also free to stop re-deciding it every morning. Let one thing you carry stay settled today — felt once, then left as it is — and see that nothing needed the argument.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a wrong that has not arrived, carrying a debt that has not been called in.
cells.ask: Take one unresolved situation and write down what each person owes. Put the page away for a day before you act on any of it.
cells.core:
Your sense of fairness has run ahead of the facts. Something is coming or something was not squared, and your body is braced to bear it — rehearsing the load, getting ready to carry a weight that may not be handed to you at all.

The compass itself is fine. What is off is the timing: it is settling accounts before they exist, and that rehearsing spends the endurance you would need if the thing did arrive. You do not have to feel your way to a verdict right now. Let the situation stay open a day. Notice what you can see without running the numbers, and let that be enough to go on.

cells.tense: The felt sense of what is right went quiet, and you have been going through motions that once came from it.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing that matters to you about a situation you both know, then let whatever they say stand without correcting it.
cells.core:
You can still carry things. You can bear what has to be borne. What is missing is the felt pull that used to tell you which of them was worth it — the line feels like something you used to have and now mostly guess at.

There is no need to push feeling back into where it went quiet; that rarely works and usually makes you flinch from the whole business. Start smaller than that. One true sentence said out loud to one person puts your own sense of fairness somewhere it can be heard again. You are not being asked to feel more. You are being asked to say one thing and let it stand.

cells.tense: You are already living by a private sense of what is fair and calling it the situation's doing.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made this week because it felt right rather than because it was required, and say "I" when you say it.
cells.core:
You are already weighing what is fair. It shows in what you refuse, in what you quietly take on, in the apology you do not make because it would be false. That weighing is running right now. You just describe it as the situation, the other person, the thing that had to be done.

What is missing is not the sense of fairness. It is you standing behind it. No announcement is required — only that you stop narrating your own judgment as the world's. When the line you hold is clearly yours, carrying it gets lighter, because you are no longer pretending you had no hand in lifting it.
